comparator.sourceNotes: Articles 7.3–7.5 of the adopted 2026–27 English EER establish 60 EC of first-year compulsory molecular and chemistry courses, 45 EC of later compulsory courses, 57 EC of differentiation with at least 18 EC from the ML1 list, a 12-EC supervised Bachelor’s Internship and Report as the final project, and 6 EC genuine free electives: 60+45+57+12+6=180. Academic Skills first-year (0 EC) and RADAr do not add credits. Three first-listed 6-EC ML1 options instantiate the 18-EC minimum without implying these particular courses are mandatory for every student. The remaining 39 EC is restricted to eligible science/medical-science bachelor courses and potentially a permitted minor; it is not filled with invented named modules. Panorama A and the English molecular philosophy instance are neutral formal choices. The prospective year-three page lists multiple 60-EC subject menus and a mandatory internship, but these illustrative lists are not stacked and do not override the adopted EER. The 2026–27 EER excludes specific overlapping Biology/Chemistry courses and three named minors; none is treated as freely interchangeable.

routeSelection.route: Molecular Life Sciences, ordinary route with neutral first-listed 18-EC ML1 selection
routeSelection.basis: The normalized target names the general English-taught Molecular Life Sciences bachelor, not one optional year-three thematic menu or an educational minor. The adopted EER specifies one shared core and a flexible differentiation phase. The first three ML1 items are neutral first-listed choices solely to instantiate the 18-EC minimum; the other 39 EC remains accurately represented as restricted selection.

alternatives.label: Molecular, cellular & biomedical life sciences
alternatives.labelReason: Molecular and cellular biology, biochemistry, physiology, genetics, disease, laboratory work, neuroscience and quantitative analysis form the visible spine; the label does not claim UCR offers the target’s chemistry sequence.
alternatives.concept: Study molecular and cellular life through biochemistry, physiology, genetics, immunity, disease, laboratory work, neurobiology and quantitative analysis. This is the strongest related-fields response to Molecular Life Sciences; it does not reproduce Radboud’s organic, inorganic, analytical and physical chemistry or its synthesis and specialist laboratory sequence.
progression: Life-science, brain-and-behaviour, programming, mathematics, statistics and data foundations precede molecular biology, physiology, laboratory work, genetics, disease, immunity, pharmacology and advanced analysis. All formal prerequisites and exact planned offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Neurobiology, brain function & biological health
alternatives.labelReason: Neurobiology, perception, cognition, development and health are integrated with molecular biology, physiology, disease and experimental methods; the label does not claim the target’s chemical or specialist imaging sequence.
alternatives.concept: Develop the target’s explicit Neurobiology direction through cellular and physiological foundations, brain biology, perception and cognition, human development, disease, mental health and experimental research. UCR supplies a coherent biological-neuroscience route but not Radboud’s chemistry spine, quantitative bioimaging or translational-neuroscience sequence.
progression: Life-science, brain-and-behaviour, data and philosophical foundations precede physiology, experimental methods, disease, perception, health psychology and advanced cognition. All formal prerequisites and exact planned offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.
alternatives.distinctness: The first programme is organised around molecular, cellular and biomedical life science with laboratory, data, imaging and pharmacology components. This route makes neurobiology, perception, cognition, development and behavioural health the organising centre. It replaces eight first-programme courses and therefore gives each programme 60 EC not found in the other, above the 30-EC floor.

questions: How do molecular and cellular processes produce biological function, disease and treatment possibilities?

candidates.label: Functional genomics & human biology
candidates.assessment: The closest programme already centres molecular-cell biology, genetics, immunity, human physiology and disease. The UCR catalogue does not support a genuinely different functional-genomics curriculum; substitutions would be cosmetic rather than a new organising direction.

candidates.label: Chemistry of life & medicinal chemistry
candidates.assessment: UCR offers Biochemistry, Pharmacology and one broad Life Science Laboratory, but no sequence in analytical, organic, inorganic or physical chemistry, synthesis, spectroscopy, crystallography or medicinal chemistry. A complete chemistry-led alternative would require unrelated filler and would misstate the defining curriculum.

selection.assessment: The molecular, cellular and biomedical programme is the strongest related-fields response. Neurobiology is an explicit stable direction and supports a distinct, feasible second programme. The next coherent direction is chemistry-led molecular and medicinal science; it fails because UCR lacks the necessary chemistry and specialist laboratory sequence, so production stops at two.

notes.text: Radboud Molecular Life Sciences integrates molecular biology with sustained organic, inorganic, analytical and physical chemistry, synthesis and several specialist laboratories. UCR can study molecular, cellular, biomedical and neurobiological questions through biology, biochemistry, data and one broad life-science laboratory, but these programmes are related-fields responses rather than reproductions of the full molecular-science curriculum.
